preamble: The alveolar trill [r] can be backed and devoiced to the voiceless velar fricative [x]. In Puerto Rican Spanish the trill phoneme /r/ (carro, rosa) is widely realized as a back fricative, velar [x] or uvular [χ]; Navarro Tomás (1948) found the alveolar trill to be the least common variant on the island, and Granda (1966) reported that the voiceless velar fricative had displaced it almost completely. In most of Brazil the Portuguese strong r, originally an alveolar trill, is pronounced as a voiceless fricative, often velar [x] (rosa [ˈxɔzɐ]).

examples.note: The backed /r/ ranges over velar [x] and uvular [χ]; it is a regional identity marker, more frequent among rural-origin speakers.
The strong r is usually a voiceless velar fricative in Brazil, alternating with [h] and [χ]; the alveolar trill survives in conservative dialects and in Africa and Asia.

sources: Arias Alvarez, A. (2025). An Acoustic Approach to Backed /r/ Realizations in Puerto Rican Spanish. Languages 10(3): 38. https://doi.org/10.3390/languages10030038

Luna, K. V. (2014). La evolución fonética y fonológica del español de Puerto Rico: de Tomás Navarro Tomás a nuestros días. Cuadernos de la ALFAL 6: 105-119. https://mundoalfal.org/sites/default/files/revista/06_cuaderno_009.pdf
